title: CONGENITAL FIBROSIS OF EXTRAOCULAR MUSCLES 3A, SYNDROMIC 1, WITH ANOSMIA AND DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY

relationships.phenotype: CONGENITAL FIBROSIS OF EXTRAOCULAR MUSCLES 3A, SYNDROMIC 1, WITH ANOSMIA AND DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles 3A, syndromic 1, with anosmia and developmental delay (CFEOM3A1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TUBB3 gene (602661) on chromosome 16q24.

checks.claim: CFEOM3A1 (congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles 3A, syndromic 1, with anosmia and developmental delay) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TUBB3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A heterozygous de novo c.1228G>A mutation (E410K) in the TUBB3 gene encoding the neuronal-specific β-tubulin isotype 3 (TUBB3) causes the TUBB3 E410K syndrome characterized by congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles (CFEOM)
checks.explanation: The abstract says a heterozygous TUBB3 mutation causes the syndrome, which matches CFEOM3A1.

checks.claim: The TUBB3 gene is located on chromosome 16q24.
checks.evidence_quote: had previously been mapped to chromosome 16q in pedigrees BN and DP (OMIM#600638, Figure S1A, Table S1A, B). The critical region for the CFEOM3 gene was 3.5 Mb and flanked by D16S498-16qter.
checks.explanation: Standard chromosomal location; consistent with the 16qter region in the paper.

paragraphs.text: CFEOM3A1 is a syndromic form of congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles caused by a recurrent de novo heterozygous mutation in the TUBB3 gene, glu410-to-lys (E410K). Affected individuals have congenital ophthalmoplegia with ptosis, congenital facial weakness, developmental delay/intellectual disability, and Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia). Other features can include vocal cord paralysis and a progressive axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy beginning later in life.

checks.claim: CFEOM3A1 is a syndromic form of congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles.
checks.evidence_quote: Missense mutations in TUBB3, the gene that encodes the neuronal-specific protein β-tubulin isotype 3, can cause isolated or syndromic congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the E410K syndrome as a syndromic form of CFEOM.

checks.claim: CFEOM3A1 is caused by a recurrent de novo heterozygous glu410-to-lys (E410K) mutation in the TUBB3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The remaining mutations, 1138C>T (R380C), 785G>A (R262H), and 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism
checks.explanation: Recurrent (six pedigrees), de novo, heterozygous E410K.

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A1 have congenital ophthalmoplegia with ptosis.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas all participants with R262H, E410K, and D417H had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness
checks.explanation: Paper defines CFEOM3 as being born with blepharoptosis and restricted eye movements.

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A1 have congenital facial weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas all participants with R262H, E410K, and D417H had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A1 have developmental delay/intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Individuals with A302T, E410K, R262H, and R380C had more severe CC dysgenesis and mild to moderate intellectual, social, and behavioral impairments.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Individuals with CFEOM3A1 have Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia).
checks.evidence_quote: expand the TUBB3 E410K phenotype to include Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Vocal cord paralysis can be a feature of CFEOM3A1.
checks.evidence_quote: in some cases, vocal cord paralysis, tracheomalacia and cyclic vomiting
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: A progressive axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy beginning later in life can be a feature of CFEOM3A1.
checks.evidence_quote: Most subjects harboring D417N and the oldest patient harboring E410K developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in the second to third decade
checks.explanation: Electromyography showed a predominantly axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy; the E410K row in the summary is described as 'likely a late-onset polyneuropathy'.

paragraphs.text: Tischfield et al. (2010) described individuals with TUBB3 mutations causing CFEOM3, either isolated or with additional features. Patients carrying the E410K substitution, which arose de novo, had CFEOM together with facial weakness, intellectual and social disabilities, and in some cases later-onset peripheral neuropathy and features of Kallmann syndrome.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) described individuals with TUBB3 mutations causing CFEOM3, either isolated or with additional features.
checks.evidence_quote: we now report that 8 different heterozygous missense mutations in TUBB3, also known as TuJ1, result in CFEOM3 in isolation or as a component of several previously undefined neurological syndromes.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: In the patients of Tischfield et al. (2010), the TUBB3 E410K substitution arose de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients carrying the TUBB3 E410K substitution had CFEOM together with facial weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas all participants with R262H, E410K, and D417H had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Patients carrying the TUBB3 E410K substitution had intellectual and social disabilities.
checks.evidence_quote: Individuals with A302T, E410K, R262H, and R380C had more severe CC dysgenesis and mild to moderate intellectual, social, and behavioral impairments.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Some patients carrying the TUBB3 E410K substitution had later-onset peripheral neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Most subjects harboring D417N and the oldest patient harboring E410K developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in the second to third decade
checks.explanation: Only the oldest E410K patient had it, which fits 'some'.

checks.claim: Some patients carrying the TUBB3 E410K substitution had features of Kallmann syndrome.
checks.explanation: Kallmann syndrome features are not mentioned in the paper.

paragraphs.text: Chew et al. (2013) characterized the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome' in a series of unrelated patients with the de novo E410K mutation. All had congenital ophthalmoplegia and congenital facial weakness, together with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia (Kallmann syndrome), developmental delay or intellectual disability, and progressive peripheral axonal neuropathy. Some had vocal cord paralysis, and cyclic vomiting was also reported. Brain imaging showed hypoplasia of the olfactory sulci/bulbs and of the oculomotor and facial nerves, but no malformations of cortical development.

checks.claim: Chew et al. (2013) characterized the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome' in a series of unrelated patients with the de novo TUBB3 E410K mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the detailed phenotypes of eight unrelated individuals who harbour this de novo mutation, and thus define the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome'.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: All patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation in the Chew et al. (2013) series had congenital ophthalmoplegia.
checks.evidence_quote: Individuals harbouring this mutation were previously reported to have congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles, facial weakness, developmental delay and possible peripheral neuropathy.
checks.explanation: CFEOM is part of the syndrome, but the abstract does not say that all patients had it.

checks.claim: All patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation in the Chew et al. (2013) series had congenital facial weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: Individuals harbouring this mutation were previously reported to have congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles, facial weakness, developmental delay and possible peripheral neuropathy.
checks.explanation: Facial weakness is part of the syndrome, but the abstract does not say that all patients had it.

checks.claim: All patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation in the Chew et al. (2013) series had hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia (Kallmann syndrome).
checks.evidence_quote: expand the TUBB3 E410K phenotype to include Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia)
checks.explanation: Kallmann syndrome is part of the phenotype, but the abstract does not say that all patients had it.

checks.claim: All patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation in the Chew et al. (2013) series had developmental delay or intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: expand the TUBB3 E410K phenotype to include Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia), stereotyped midface hypoplasia, intellectual disabilities
checks.explanation: Intellectual disability is part of the phenotype, but the abstract does not say that all patients had it.

checks.claim: All patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation in the Chew et al. (2013) series had progressive peripheral axonal neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We now confirm by electrophysiology that a progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy does indeed segregate with the mutation
checks.explanation: A progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy is stated. The abstract does not specify that it is axonal or that all patients had it.

checks.claim: Some patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation in the Chew et al. (2013) series had vocal cord paralysis.
checks.evidence_quote: in some cases, vocal cord paralysis, tracheomalacia and cyclic vomiting
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Cyclic vomiting was reported in patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation in the Chew et al. (2013) series.
checks.evidence_quote: in some cases, vocal cord paralysis, tracheomalacia and cyclic vomiting
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation showed hypoplasia of the olfactory sulci/bulbs.
checks.evidence_quote: hypoplastic to absent olfactory sulci, olfactory bulbs and oculomotor and facial nerves
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation showed hypoplasia of the oculomotor and facial nerves.
checks.evidence_quote: hypoplastic to absent olfactory sulci, olfactory bulbs and oculomotor and facial nerves
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation showed no malformations of cortical development.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions a thin corpus callosum and anterior commissure but says nothing about whether cortical malformations were present. This may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

paragraphs.text: The E410K mutation in TUBB3 arose de novo in reported patients (Tischfield et al., 2010; Chew et al., 2013), consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: The TUBB3 E410K mutation arose de novo in reported patients.
checks.evidence_quote: 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The de novo occurrence of the TUBB3 E410K mutation is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of CFEOM3A1.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified TUBB3 as the mutated gene underlying a series of autosomal dominant disorders of axon guidance that we collectively call the TUBB3 syndromes.
checks.explanation: The paper calls the TUBB3 syndromes autosomal dominant and says the severe forms usually arise de novo.

paragraphs.text: In patients with syndromic CFEOM3, Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a de novo heterozygous E410K mutation in the TUBB3 gene. Functional studies of TUBB3 mutations showed altered microtubule dynamics and impaired interaction with kinesin motors, and the authors proposed that this disrupts axon guidance.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a de novo heterozygous E410K mutation in the TUBB3 gene in patients with syndromic CFEOM3.
checks.evidence_quote: 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism
checks.explanation: Found in heterozygous form in probands with CFEOM plus additional neurological symptoms.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Tischfield et al. (2010) showed that TUBB3 mutations alter microtubule dynamics.
checks.evidence_quote: Modeling each mutation in yeast tubulin demonstrates that all alter dynamic instability whereas a subset disrupts the interaction of microtubules with kinesin motors.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Tischfield et al. (2010) showed that TUBB3 mutations impair interaction with kinesin motors.
checks.evidence_quote: Modeling each mutation in yeast tubulin demonstrates that all alter dynamic instability whereas a subset disrupts the interaction of microtubules with kinesin motors.
checks.explanation: Only a subset of the mutations, including E410K, impaired kinesin interactions; the claim is worded for TUBB3 mutations in general.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) proposed that the altered microtubule dynamics and kinesin interactions caused by TUBB3 mutations disrupt axon guidance.
checks.evidence_quote: These findings demonstrate that normal TUBB3 is required for axon guidance and maintenance in mammals.
checks.explanation: The authors connect the functional defects to impaired axon guidance.

paragraphs.text: Chew et al. (2013) identified the same recurrent de novo heterozygous E410K mutation in TUBB3 in all patients in their series and defined the associated syndrome.

checks.claim: Chew et al. (2013) identified the recurrent de novo heterozygous E410K mutation in TUBB3 in all patients in their series.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the detailed phenotypes of eight unrelated individuals who harbour this de novo mutation, and thus define the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome'.
checks.explanation: The same de novo E410K mutation is reported in all eight individuals, but the abstract does not state that it is heterozygous.

checks.claim: Chew et al. (2013) defined the syndrome associated with the TUBB3 E410K mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the detailed phenotypes of eight unrelated individuals who harbour this de novo mutation, and thus define the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome'.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that different TUBB3 substitutions produced different phenotypes. Some, such as R262C, could cause isolated CFEOM3 that was often inherited. The E410K substitution caused a recognizable syndrome with facial weakness, intellectual disability, Kallmann syndrome, and later-onset neuropathy.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that different TUBB3 substitutions produced different phenotypes.
checks.evidence_quote: Notably, these substitutions can result in diagnostically distinct phenotypes (Figure 5F)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Some TUBB3 substitutions, such as R262C, could cause isolated CFEOM3.
checks.evidence_quote: Overall, most adults with isolated CFEOM3 have R262C or, less commonly, R62Q or A302T substitutions.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Isolated CFEOM3 caused by TUBB3 substitutions such as R262C was often inherited.
checks.evidence_quote: while the TUBB3 phenotypes limited to CFEOM3 and polyneuropathy often segregate in autosomal dominant families, those with more severe clinical findings typically arise de novo.
checks.explanation: Isolated CFEOM3 often segregates in families; R262C was found in 11 pedigrees.

checks.claim: The TUBB3 E410K substitution caused a recognizable syndrome with facial weakness, intellectual disability, Kallmann syndrome, and later-onset neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Association of severe CFEOM3 with facial weakness, developmental delay, moderate to severe CC dysgenesis and likely a late-onset polyneuropathy predicts the E410K substitution
checks.explanation: Facial weakness, developmental delay and late-onset neuropathy are supported; Kallmann syndrome is not mentioned in the paper.

paragraphs.text: In patients with CFEOM3 accompanied by facial weakness, intellectual disability, and Kallmann syndrome, Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a de novo heterozygous c.1228G-A transition in the TUBB3 gene, resulting in a glu410-to-lys (E410K) substitution.

checks.claim: Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a de novo heterozygous c.1228G-A transition in the TUBB3 gene, resulting in a glu410-to-lys (E410K) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism
checks.explanation: The paper reports these as heterozygous de novo changes.

checks.claim: The patients with the TUBB3 c.1228G-A (E410K) mutation reported by Tischfield et al. (2010) had CFEOM3 accompanied by facial weakness, intellectual disability, and Kallmann syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Association of severe CFEOM3 with facial weakness, developmental delay, moderate to severe CC dysgenesis and likely a late-onset polyneuropathy predicts the E410K substitution
checks.explanation: CFEOM3, facial weakness and intellectual impairment are supported; Kallmann syndrome is not mentioned.

paragraphs.text: Chew et al. (2013) reported additional unrelated patients with the de novo E410K mutation and defined the TUBB3 E410K syndrome.

checks.claim: Chew et al. (2013) reported additional unrelated patients with the de novo TUBB3 E410K mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: We report the detailed phenotypes of eight unrelated individuals who harbour this de novo mutation
checks.explanation: The abstract describes these as further patients beyond those previously reported.

checks.claim: Chew et al. (2013) defined the TUBB3 E410K syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: and thus define the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome'
checks.explanation: Stated directly.
